cited_details.statement: A 2022 paper states that digital watermarking requires high robustness and high invisibility https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13801.
A 2019 study incorporated deep learning networks with image watermarking https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11331.
The same paper describes that a robust image watermarking system keeps the watermark intact under a designated class of distortions https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11331.
A 2020 paper states that modern image watermarking research primarily focuses on multi-bit scenarios that extract the entire communicative watermark https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02460.

A 2020 study proposed a general deep neural network based watermarking method that trains on an image set and uses the trained model to protect a distinct test image set in a bulk manner https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12428.
The same study notes that technologies of the Internet of Things facilitate digital contents such as images being acquired in a massive way https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12428.
A 2021 study proposed a light-weight deep convolutional autoencoder architecture to embed a secret image inside a cover image https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2021.3113953.
The architecture extracts the embedded secret image from the stego image https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2021.3113953.
The method was evaluated using three datasets: COCO, CelebA, and ImageNet https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2021.3113953.
Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio, hiding capacity, and imperceptibility results on the test set were used to measure performance https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2021.3113953.
A 2021 paper proposes a compact neural network-based algorithm for robust image watermarking https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.13491.

The paper states that digital image watermarking seeks to protect digital media information from unauthorized access, where the message is embedded into the digital image and extracted from it https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.13491.

A separate study presents a novel end-to-end solution for embedding and recovering the watermark in the digital image using convolutional neural networks https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b1ffb4adfc9ec647d5dee15cd3dacce1a662ffe5.
The approach applies spreading https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b1ffb4adfc9ec647d5dee15cd3dacce1a662ffe5.

A 2023 study offers a robust zero watermarking strategy for medical pictures based on an Improved NasNet-Mobile convolutional neural network and the discrete cosine transform https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics12163444.

The study modified the pre-trained NasNet-Mobile structure using a fully connected layer with 128 output and a regression layer instead of the original Softmax layer and classification layer https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics12163444.
Transfer learning was performed on the modified network to extract 128 features from medical images https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics12163444.
A 2022 paper introduced DBMark for deep boosting the robustness of DNN-based image watermarking https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13801.
The paper notes that least significant bits (LSB) was the earliest research on image information hiding https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13801.

A 2023 study addresses the lack of robustness of existing medical image watermarking algorithms by combining an Improved NasNet-Mobile network with the discrete cosine transform https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics12163444.
A 2015 paper presents a thorough literature review of robust digital image watermarking applied in diverse applications https://doi.org/10.1080/02564602.2015.1042927.
The review studies classification of various watermarking schemes with their properties and applications in different domains https://doi.org/10.1080/02564602.2015.1042927.
A 2004 paper presents a high capacity reversible watermarking scheme using companding technique over integer DCT coefficients of image blocks https://doi.org/10.1117/12.527216.
The scheme chooses AC coefficients in the integer DCT domain for the bit-shift operation https://doi.org/10.1117/12.527216.

A 2021 paper titled "Watermark Faker: Towards Forgery of Digital Image Watermarking" was authored by researchers at the College of Computer Science, Sichuan University https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.12489.
A 2023 paper titled "PTW: Pivotal Tuning Watermarking for Pre-Trained Image Generators" addresses deepfakes https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07361.
The paper defines deepfakes as content synthesized using deep generators https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07361.
The paper notes that deepfakes, when misused, have the potential to erode trust in digital media https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07361.
